quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Tom woke up early in the morning. He ate a bowl of cereal for breakfast. Then he put on his shoes and left for school.
options: Tom woke up early in the morning.
Tom ate cereal for breakfast.
Tom put on his shoes and left for school.
Tom watched television all morning.
quests.hint: Look for the morning order: waking, eating, then leaving. One frame does not match the story.
quests.explanation: Morning routine stories follow a natural sequence: waking, eating, and departing. The distractor replaces departure with a stay-at-home activity.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Sarah went to the market with her mother. They bought apples and bread. When they got home, Sarah helped put the food away.
options: Sarah cooked dinner all by herself.
Sarah and her mother went to the market.
They bought apples and bread.
Sarah helped put the food away at home.
quests.hint: Trace the steps: going to market, buying food, then arriving home. One option invents an event.
quests.explanation: Shopping stories follow: travel, purchase, and return. The distractor introduces a cooking event that never occurred.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The teacher wrote new words on the board. The students copied them into their notebooks. After class, they practised spelling the words aloud.
options: The teacher wrote new words on the board.
Students copied the words into notebooks.
The students went on a school field trip.
Students practised spelling the words after class.
quests.hint: Look for the classroom sequence: writing, copying, then practising. One frame belongs to a different activity.
quests.explanation: Classroom learning sequences move from teacher input to student recording to student practice. The distractor replaces revision with an outing.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Ben found a puppy sitting near the park gate. He gave it water and a biscuit. Then he took the puppy home to keep it safe.
options: Ben found a puppy at the park gate.
Ben returned the puppy to a pet shop.
He gave the puppy water and a biscuit.
Ben took the puppy home to keep it safe.
quests.hint: Follow the events: finding the puppy, caring for it, and the final decision. One option changes the outcome.
quests.explanation: Rescue narratives move from discovery to care to resolution. The distractor changes the final action.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Maria put on her coat and scarf. She walked to the bus stop at the end of the street. The bus arrived and she climbed on board.
options: Maria put on her coat and scarf.
She walked to the bus stop.
Maria climbed on the bus when it arrived.
Maria drove her car to work.
quests.hint: Track the travel sequence: dressing warmly, walking to the stop, then boarding. One frame changes the mode of transport.
quests.explanation: Travel preparation stories follow: dressing, walking to transport, and boarding. The distractor replaces the bus with a car.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Jake opened his lunchbox and took out a sandwich. He ate it slowly while talking to his friends. After lunch, he went back to class.
options: Jake skipped lunch and went to the library.
Jake opened his lunchbox.
Jake ate his sandwich while talking to friends.
Jake went back to class after lunch.
quests.hint: Find the lunchtime sequence: opening the box, eating and chatting, then returning. One frame skips the main activity.
quests.explanation: Lunchtime narratives move from unpacking food to eating and socialising to returning to lessons. The distractor skips eating entirely.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: On Saturday morning, Dan rode his bicycle to the park. He played football with his friends for an hour. Afterwards, they all had ice cream together.
options: Dan rode his bicycle to the park.
He played football with his friends.
Dan stayed at home and read a book instead.
They had ice cream together afterwards.
quests.hint: Trace the Saturday activity: riding to the park, playing sport, then the reward. One frame contradicts the whole outing.
quests.explanation: Weekend activity stories follow: travel, activity, and social reward. The distractor replaces the outing with a stay-at-home activity.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Mia noticed her plant was drooping. She watered it carefully and moved it closer to the window. Two days later, the plant looked healthy again.
options: Mia noticed the plant was drooping.
Mia threw the dead plant in the bin.
She watered it and moved it to the window.
The plant was healthy again two days later.
quests.hint: Look for the cause and effect: noticing the problem, taking action, then seeing the result. One frame shows the wrong outcome.
quests.explanation: Problem-solution stories move from noticing to acting to resolving. The distractor replaces recovery with disposal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The postman delivered a large package to the door. Amy signed for it and brought it inside. She opened it and found a birthday present from her aunt.
options: The postman delivered a package to the door.
Amy signed for it and brought it inside.
Amy found a birthday present inside the box.
Amy refused to accept the delivery.
quests.hint: Sequence the delivery: receiving at the door, bringing it in, then opening it. One frame changes the response entirely.
quests.explanation: Delivery narratives progress from arrival to acceptance to discovery. The distractor introduces refusal, which reverses the expected sequence.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The children planted seeds in the school garden. Every day they watered the soil and checked for growth. After three weeks, small green shoots appeared.
options: The seeds never grew because the soil was too dry.
The children planted seeds in the school garden.
They watered and checked the soil every day.
Green shoots appeared after three weeks.
quests.hint: Follow the gardening process: planting, caring daily, then the result. One frame gives the wrong outcome.
quests.explanation: Growth narratives follow a time sequence: planting, nurturing, and producing results. The distractor shows failure instead of success.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Dad checked the weather forecast and saw it would rain. He took an umbrella before leaving the house. He stayed dry all the way to work.
options: Dad checked the weather forecast for rain.
Dad took an umbrella before leaving.
Dad was completely soaked by the rain.
Dad stayed completely dry on his way to work.
quests.hint: Sequence the preparation: checking the forecast, taking an umbrella, then the outcome. The distractor gives the wrong result.
quests.explanation: Preparation stories show a cause-and-effect chain: checking information, acting on it, and experiencing the benefit.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Anna felt sick and told her teacher. The teacher called Anna's parents. Her mother came to school and took her to the doctor.
options: Anna felt sick and told her teacher.
Anna rested in class and felt better.
The teacher called Anna's parents.
Anna's mother took her to the doctor.
quests.hint: Follow the health sequence: reporting illness, the teacher's response, then what happened. One frame skips the parental response.
quests.explanation: Health emergency narratives show reporting a problem, contacting others, and receiving medical care as the natural three stages.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Kevin saved his pocket money for three weeks. He went to the toy shop and chose a remote-control car. He paid at the counter and took it home.
options: Kevin saved his pocket money for three weeks.
He chose a remote-control car at the toy shop.
Kevin paid and took the car home.
Kevin spent all his money on sweets at school.
quests.hint: Trace the saving story: gathering money, making a choice, then completing the purchase. The distractor changes how the money was spent.
quests.explanation: Saving narratives follow a goal-directed path: saving, selecting, and purchasing the desired item.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Grace wrote a letter to her grandmother. She folded it, put it in an envelope, and wrote the address. Then she walked to the post box and sent it.
options: Grace called her grandmother on the phone.
Grace wrote a letter to her grandmother.
She folded it and addressed the envelope.
Grace walked to the post box and sent the letter.
quests.hint: Follow the letter sequence: writing, preparing the envelope, then posting. One frame replaces the letter with a phone call.
quests.explanation: Postal narratives show the full process: composing, preparing, and dispatching. The distractor replaces a physical letter with a digital alternative.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The fire alarm rang loudly in the school building. Everyone walked quickly and calmly to the exit. The students lined up in the playground.
options: The fire alarm rang in the school.
Everyone walked quickly to the exit.
The students hid under their desks.
Students lined up in the playground.
quests.hint: Sequence the safety drill: the alarm, walking out, then gathering in the playground. One frame shows the wrong safety response.
quests.explanation: Emergency procedure stories show alert, evacuation, and assembly as the three required stages. The distractor replaces evacuation with hiding.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The library opened at nine o'clock. Jack walked in and chose three books from the shelf. He borrowed them using his library card.
options: The library opened at nine o'clock.
Jack bought the books from the library shop.
Jack chose three books from the shelf.
Jack borrowed the books with his library card.
quests.hint: Follow the library visit: opening time, selecting books, then borrowing. One frame confuses borrowing with buying.
quests.explanation: Library visit narratives show access, selection, and borrowing as the three natural steps. The distractor confuses a free service with a paid one.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The team decided to paint the community wall. They bought paint in five colours and prepared their brushes. By evening, the mural was finished.
options: The team decided to paint the community wall.
They bought paint and prepared their brushes.
The mural was finished by evening.
The council refused permission to paint the wall.
quests.hint: Trace the mural project: deciding, preparing, then completing. One frame shows an obstacle not mentioned in the story.
quests.explanation: Community project stories follow a decision-to-completion arc. The distractor introduces a refusal that does not appear in the narrative.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Lily lost her hat on the way home from school. She retraced her steps back to the park. She found it hanging on a bench near the gate.
options: Lily bought a new hat at the shop.
Lily lost her hat on the way home from school.
She retraced her steps back to the park.
Lily found her hat on a bench near the gate.
quests.hint: Follow the lost-and-found story: losing, searching, then finding. One frame shows a different solution.
quests.explanation: Lost-and-found narratives have three stages: loss, search, and recovery. The distractor replaces recovery with a new purchase.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Paul woke up and realised he had overslept. He quickly washed his face and grabbed his school bag. He ran all the way to the bus stop and just caught the bus.
options: Paul woke up and realised he had overslept.
He washed his face and grabbed his bag quickly.
Paul decided to stay home from school.
Paul ran to the bus stop and caught the bus just in time.
quests.hint: Track the rushed morning: waking late, preparing quickly, then catching the bus. The distractor replaces success with giving up.
quests.explanation: Last-minute narratives show a problem, a quick response, and a just-in-time resolution. The distractor replaces resolution with avoidance.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The old bridge was damaged in the storm. Workers came to inspect it the next day. They closed the bridge for repairs and set up a detour.
options: The old bridge was damaged in the storm.
The bridge was immediately demolished by the council.
Workers came to inspect the bridge the next day.
The bridge was closed and a detour was set up.
quests.hint: Sequence the infrastructure event: storm damage, inspection, then the official response. One frame exaggerates the action taken.
quests.explanation: Infrastructure narratives follow report-assess-respond. The distractor replaces a temporary solution with a permanent and drastic one.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The baby started crying in the middle of the night. Mum got up and checked if the baby was hungry. She fed the baby and it settled back to sleep.
options: The baby started crying in the middle of the night.
Mum got up and checked on the baby.
Mum fed the baby and it went back to sleep.
The baby slept quietly through the entire night.
quests.hint: Look for the night sequence: crying, checking, then settling. The distractor contradicts the opening event entirely.
quests.explanation: Care narratives show a response to a need: signal, investigation, and resolution. The distractor eliminates the problem before it starts.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The supermarket was very busy on Saturday morning. Emma grabbed a basket and walked through each aisle carefully. At the checkout she paid with her bank card.
options: Emma ordered her groceries online from home.
The supermarket was very busy on Saturday morning.
Emma walked through each aisle with her basket.
Emma paid at the checkout with her bank card.
quests.hint: Follow the shopping trip: arriving, browsing aisles, then paying. One frame replaces the in-store visit with online shopping.
quests.explanation: In-store shopping narratives show arrival, selection, and payment. The distractor replaces the physical visit with a remote one.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The school sports day was held in the morning. The children ran races and competed in long jump. The winning team was awarded a trophy at the end.
options: The school sports day was held in the morning.
Children ran races and competed in long jump.
The sports day was cancelled because of heavy rain.
The winning team was awarded a trophy.
quests.hint: Trace the sports day: the event itself, the activities, then the ceremony. One frame cancels the event.
quests.explanation: Event narratives follow beginning-activity-conclusion. The distractor cancels the event rather than allowing it to conclude naturally.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Dad noticed the kitchen tap was dripping constantly. He called a plumber who arrived within the hour. The plumber fixed the tap and the dripping stopped.
options: Dad noticed the kitchen tap was dripping.
Dad replaced the entire kitchen sink himself.
A plumber arrived within the hour.
The plumber fixed the tap and the dripping stopped.
quests.hint: Follow the repair story: noticing the problem, calling help, then the fix. One frame exaggerates the repair needed.
quests.explanation: Repair narratives show problem identification, calling for professional help, and successful resolution as three stages.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Chloe wanted to learn to swim. She signed up for lessons at the local pool. After six weeks of practice, she could swim the full length of the pool.
options: Chloe signed up for swimming lessons at the pool.
She practised at the pool for six weeks.
Chloe could swim the full length of the pool.
Chloe was too afraid of water to enter the pool.
quests.hint: Trace the learning journey: signing up, practising consistently, then achieving the goal. The distractor contradicts the achievement.
quests.explanation: Learning narratives follow enrolment, practice, and mastery. The distractor introduces fear that prevents progress.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The café opened a new outdoor seating area. They added colourful tables and string lights. Customers quickly began to enjoy the new space.
options: The café closed due to falling customer numbers.
The café opened a new outdoor seating area.
They added colourful tables and string lights.
Customers quickly began to enjoy the space.
quests.hint: Sequence the café story: opening the area, decorating it, then the customer response. One frame replaces a positive outcome with a negative one.
quests.explanation: Business improvement stories show a change, its decoration, and a positive response. The distractor replaces success with failure.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Rosa found a recipe online for chocolate cake. She gathered all the ingredients and mixed them together. She baked the cake for thirty minutes and served it warm.
options: Rosa found a chocolate cake recipe online.
She gathered all the ingredients and mixed them.
Rosa bought a ready-made cake from the shop.
Rosa baked the cake and served it warm.
quests.hint: Follow the baking sequence: finding the recipe, preparing, then baking. One frame skips the homemade process entirely.
quests.explanation: Cooking narratives follow plan, prepare, and produce. The distractor replaces the act of cooking with a ready-made purchase.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The school choir practised a new song every Tuesday. They rehearsed carefully for a whole month. At the winter concert, they performed it to great applause.
options: The school choir practised a new song each Tuesday.
The winter concert was cancelled at the last minute.
They rehearsed carefully for an entire month.
The choir performed the song at the winter concert.
quests.hint: Trace the choir story: weekly practice, a month of preparation, then the performance. One frame cancels the event.
quests.explanation: Preparation narratives show repeated practice, a build-up period, and a public performance. The distractor cancels the final event.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The neighbours organised a street party. They hung bunting and set up tables along the road. Everyone brought food to share and had a wonderful afternoon.
options: The neighbours organised a street party.
They hung bunting and set up tables outside.
Everyone brought food and enjoyed the afternoon.
The neighbours complained about the noise of the party.
quests.hint: Follow the party story: organising it, decorating, then the shared celebration. One frame introduces conflict not mentioned in the story.
quests.explanation: Community event narratives show planning, preparation, and celebration. The distractor replaces a joyful outcome with a conflict.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: James forgot his homework at home. He phoned his dad and asked him to bring it to school. His dad arrived just before the lesson started.
options: James pretended he had already handed in his homework.
James forgot his homework at home.
He phoned his dad and asked him to bring it.
His dad arrived at school just before the lesson.
quests.hint: Follow the problem-solving story: forgetting, calling for help, then the rescue. One frame shows dishonesty instead of action.
quests.explanation: Problem-solving narratives show identifying a problem, seeking help, and receiving it just in time. The distractor replaces honesty with deception.
